Name: Gold to Mithril
Author: Shiroho
Description:
[b][color=#000000][size=3][u]INTRODUCTION[/u][/size][/color][/b]

﻿Like [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/7309]Gold to titanium[/url] mod created by [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/users/85371353]Olioleander[/url] I do believe that gold should not appear as a component for tools since it's far to be robust and can almost be bend by human strength depending of the object thickness. It would not resist the strikes you could make with this pickaxe that's for sure!

﻿﻿So this mod replaces most of the gold instances in the game by objects made of mithril including descriptions and displayed names. Like many popular D&D/fantasy related stories or novels including Tolkien's, It is know that mithril is a silver-ish metal that have something around blue/cyan/green colors sub-hues and is very bright. 

﻿Titanium was indeed a great candidat, but I run the game with another mod that already recolor iridium with something that has a blue hue very close to it ([url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/4366]Iridium recolor mod[/url] if you are curious, where I love the Sky or Teal colors setup for my endgame tools) so I had to imagine something else and make my own gold recolor mod, with something closer to a green or cyan hue and then there is how the Mithril idea jumped to my face. And this time, no one can say mithril is a soft metal !
 
[color=#000000][size=3][b][u]HOW TO INSTALL [/u][/b][/size][/color]

[b]STEP [color=#c27ba0]0[/color][/b] : Make sure you have SMAPI and Content patcher installed for the last version. This mods is 1.6 ready!
[b]STEP [color=#c27ba0]1[/color][/b] : Download the file, extract it in mod folder of your game.[b][color=#6fa8dc][size=3][url=https://reshade.me/]
[/url][/size][/color]STEP [color=#c27ba0]2[/color][/b] : That's it!? Well now hope to step on one of them soon and enjoy!


[b][color=#000000][size=3][u]SPECIAL THANKS[/u][/size][/color][/b]

﻿I really have to thanks [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/users/85371353]Olioleander[/url] for showing me the way to do that properly and also helped my desire/idea to germinate.
